an4.27:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four trifles, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.3: (1) “A rag-robe is a trifle among robes, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.4: (2) A lump of almsfood is a trifle among meals, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.5: (3) The foot of a tree is a trifle among lodgings, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.6: (4) Putrid urine is a trifle among medicines, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.7: “These are the four trifles, easily gained and blameless.
an4.27:1.8: When a bhikkhu is satisfied with what is trifling and easily gained, I say that he has one of the factors of the ascetic life.”
an4.27:2.1: When one is content with what is blameless,
an4.27:2.3: when one’s mind is not distressed
an4.27:3.2: to conform to the ascetic life,
